writing.overall_comment: The SKILL.md is well organized and practical, but it would be stronger with precise script paths, safer examples, and tighter alignment between its broad Xcode claims and its file-addition focus.

dimensions.name: Semantic accuracy
dimensions.comment: The name and description correctly identify Xcode project management and .pbxproj/file-addition automation, though 'expert' and broad iOS/macOS workflow claims slightly exceed the script-focused content.

dimensions.name: Examples & edge cases
dimensions.comment: Examples cover common workflows, dry runs, exit codes, and troubleshooting, but several shell snippets are fragile or misaligned on paths (e.g., ORIG_HEAD, comm/grep, scripts/ vs project root).

dimensions.name: Actionability
dimensions.comment: The workflows provide explicit commands and checklists, but ambiguous script locations and auto-detection assumptions leave readers unsure how to execute the tool reliably.

suggestions: In the examples, resolve the `scripts/` vs project-root ambiguity by documenting a single expected working directory and updating every command path to match it.

For the `ORIG_HEAD`, `comm`, and `grep` snippets, add explicit guards and fallbacks (e.g., checking `ORIG_HEAD` exists and handling empty `grep`/`comm` output) so the examples do not fail in edge cases.
In the usage/setup section, state the auto-detection assumptions and provide an explicit override or prerequisite checklist so readers know how to execute the tool reliably.
